diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Following \citet[Chapter 6]{applebaum2004}, the stronger condition $B_{\ell}\geq2$ is necessary to guarantee the
existence of a unique solution with finite variance to the stochastic
differential equation (\ref{eq: intro - asset prices dynamics}).

issues.failure_explanation: The claim states that X has finite moments up to order k if and only if ∫e^{k‖z‖}ℓ(dz)<∞. This is false in the 'only if' direction. The correct criterion for E[e^{jL^{(i)}}]<∞ (and hence for moments of X of order j) involves directional exponential moments ∫e^{jz^{(i)}}ℓ(dz)<∞, which is strictly weaker than ∫e^{k‖z‖}ℓ(dz)<∞ because e^{kz^{(i)}} can be far smaller than e^{k‖z‖} when z^{(i)}<0. Moreover, the right-hand side depends on the choice of norm ‖·‖ while moment existence is norm-independent. Concrete counterexample: the VG0 parameter set (α=0) yields B_ℓ≈0.94 in the ρ-norm, so ∫e^{‖z‖_ρ}ℓ(dz) diverges, yet the Gamma subordinator has moments of all orders, so E[(X^{(i)})^j]<∞ for every j. The downstream consequence is the claim that k<B_ℓ is a necessary condition for moments up to order k, and the related claim that B_ℓ≥2 is 'necessary' for well-posedness with finite variance: both overstate the strength of B_ℓ as a requirement.

failure_location.quote: Since the process $X$ has finite moments of all orders up to $k\in\mathbb{N}$  if and only if  $\int_{\left\Vert z\right\Vert >\epsilon}e^{k\left\Vert z\right\Vert }\ell\left(dz\right)<\infty$ for any $\epsilon>0$, then $k<B_\ell$  provides a necessary condition of it.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 'if and only if' characterization with the correct sufficient condition (e.g., ∫e^{kz^{(i)}}ℓ(dz)<∞ for each i implies moments up to order k), and weaken the claim that B_ℓ≥2 is necessary to state that it is a sufficient condition ensuring well-posedness via the cited result. The assumption B_ℓ>2 can remain in the model as a sufficient condition.
issues.overall_effect: The stated necessary condition on B_ℓ for finite moments and well-posedness is wrong. The model assumption B_ℓ>2 is sufficient but not necessary; the VG0 experiments (B_ℓ<2 in the ρ-norm) are outside the stated assumption yet produce valid results, creating a self-inconsistency between the theory and the experiments. No formal result or algorithm is affected.
issues.title: False moment characterization equating finiteness of moments with convergence of full exponential integral
issues.why_classification: A local correction to one sentence (changing 'if and only if' to 'if' or substituting the correct exponential-moment condition) and a wording change on 'necessary' preserves the model assumptions, the numerical method, and all results. No new lemma or construction is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The variance of the NTS process is derived as V[L(1)] = ηη^⊤V[G(1)] + ρE[G(1)] = ηη^⊤·δΓ(2−α)/λ^{2−α} + ρ·δΓ(1−α)/λ^{1−α}. Factoring out δΓ(2−α)/λ^{2−α} and using Γ(2−α) = (1−α)Γ(1−α) gives the coefficient ρ·λ/(1−α) + ηη^⊤, as stated in Table 'Main quantities of the Normal Tempered Stable process' in the appendix. The main text instead displays ρλ^{1−α} + ηη^⊤. These differ whenever α ≠ 0 and λ ≠ 1; e.g. for α = 1/2, λ = 20766.4 (set NIG0), λ/(1−α) = 41533 while λ^{1−α} ≈ 144, a factor of ~288 discrepancy. The numerical values in Table 2 (standard deviations and correlations) are consistent with the correct appendix formula ρλ/(1−α), not with the displayed main-text formula, confirming the main text is wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ρλ^{1−α} with ρλ/(1−α) in the variance formula in the numerical-experiments section so that it agrees with the correct formula in the appendix table and with the derivation V[L] = ηη^⊤V[G] + ρE[G].
issues.overall_effect: A reader who relies on the displayed main-text formula will compute wrong variances and correlations for any NTS parameter set with α ≠ 0 (e.g., both NIG sets). Table 2's numerical values are correct (computed with the appendix formula), so no result in the paper is numerically affected, but the stated formula is a false mathematical claim about the NTS process.
issues.title: Variance formula for the NTS process contains wrong factor ρλ^{1−α} instead of ρλ/(1−α)
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single local replacement of one factor in one displayed formula to match the correct formula already given in the appendix. All computations, tables, and conclusions remain valid without any change to arguments, constructions, or guarantees.
